summary: Ephemeral 5xx wave after tenant scale-up: connection queueing causing runtime GPU pagefaults
description: Issue summary: BrightChat reported a ~3 minute burst of 5xx responses (predominantly 502 and 503) at ~2026-03-10T05:22Z immediately after a scheduled tenant capacity scale-up. Impact: customer traffic experienced request failures and degraded streaming sessions resulting in user-visible timeouts and elevated error counts. Environment: Dedicated pool in prod-us-west; scale-up event triggered by scheduled policy for increased reserved replicas. Immediate symptoms included API gateway spikes in connection queuing and high upstream failure rates. Observed behavior: API gateway reported connection queue depth growing to >1200 connections for the tenant route, per-tenant token bucket exhaustion, and spikes of runtime process exits with GPU pagefault/backtrace logs. Expected behavior: scale-up should increase capacity without transient connection storms or runtime panics. This ticket centralizes customer-facing investigation, mitigation, and follow-up actions.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Schedule a capacity increase for a dedicated tenant pool (mirror BrightChat's policy: +3 replicas over 30s with warmup enabled).
2) Replay short streaming sessions at 250 requests/sec with ~50ms inter-request intervals from 200 distinct client sockets to simulate small streaming connections.
3) Observe gateway connection queue metrics, per-tenant token bucket rates, and runtime logs during the warmup window.
4) Note any 5xx spike correlated with queue depth or runtime OOM/pagefaults.
logs: 2026-03-10T05:22:21Z runtime[pid=8873] CRIT gpu_page_fault at 0x7f9a2b13f000 backtrace=... kernel: nvidia_uvm: NvUvmReadPage failed
2026-03-10T05:22:22Z runtime INFO process_exit pid=8873 signal=SIGSEGV reason=gpu_page_fault
2026-03-10T05:22:25Z autoscaler INFO scaling_event tenant=brightchat old_replicas=2 target_replicas=5 reason=scheduled_policy
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: warmup/scale-up caused a rapid influx of connections that saturated API gateway per-tenant queues; queued requests were replayed to upstream runtimes producing KV cache contention and GPU driver page faults.
Metric evidence: tenant token-bucket rate dropped to 0 briefly; apigw connection_queue_depth correlated tightly with 502 spikes (r=0.87).
Runtime logs show repeated GPU pagefault signatures (nvidia_uvm read failures) across multiple processes on the new nodes started during scale-up window.

Checked node health: new replicas launched on hosts with driver version 535.86.05; older hosts are on 535.54.03. Suspect driver mismatch and memory pressure interplay with many small streaming sessions.
No recent model changes. Request sizes small but concurrency extremely bursty due to many short-lived connections.
actions_taken: 2026-03-10T05:24Z: Applied emergency per-tenant connection cap at API gateway (cap=300) for brightchat to prevent further connection storm.
2026-03-10T05:26Z: Temporarily disabled aggressive keepalive reuse on gateway for tenant to reduce queued sockets.
2026-03-10T05:29Z: Rolled back scheduled warmup to hold at prior replica count while investigation continues.
2026-03-10T07:10Z: Customer notified with interim workaround and monitoring window.
resolution: Mitigation in place: per-tenant cap restored and scheduled scale-up paused. Root cause appears to be interaction between rapid scale-up, high short-lived connection burst patterns, and a GPU driver variant on new hosts causing pagefaults under certain memory access patterns. Next steps: (1) engineering to reproduce with driver 535.86.05 and submit kernel/driver issue if reproducible; (2) add apigw circuit-breaker logic to throttle new-socket arrival rate during scale events; (3) update autoscaler warmup to stagger replica addition and pre-warm KV cache asynchronously; (4) coordinate host fleet to homogenize driver versions. Target follow-up ETA: 2026-03-18. Customer asked to keep monitoring; no permanent customer-impacting downtime observed after mitigation.
